materials: Printed on: 2019-10-02 Page 4 of 8 - Boil mixture until agarose is completely dissolved (Note: cap must be untightened!). Let bottle cool at room temperature. - When agarose temperature is <50°C (hold in your hand), add 7 µL Ethidium Bromide solution per 100 mL agarose gel. (If too hot, ethidium bromide may be degraded.) - Mix well and cast gel. Remove bubbles with a tip if needed. Let solidify at room temperature. LOADING AND RUNNING THE GEL 1. Add 10 µL of 6x Crystal Violet loading dye to 50 µL of DNA sample and load app. 20 µL onto gel. 2. Run gel at 35V for 10 minutes and then at 50V for 20 minutes. A thin violet band should be visible, moving down into the gel. If no band is visible, insufficient DNA was loaded (< 200 ng). 3. If DNA bands is sufficiently separated so that the fragment is easily excised, switch power supply off. Proceed directly to Excision of DNA. The correct fragment size is ca. 2300 bp. If the main fragment is clearly below or above that size, do not use for purification but repeat PCR. EXCISING DNA 1. Transfer the gel onto saran wrap. 3. Using a new scalpel, carefully excise the correct DNA fragment from the gel. 4. Transfer the excised agarose plug to a sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube. PURIFYING DNA FRAGMENT 1. Weigh gel slice. 2. For each 100 mg of agarose gel add 200 µL Buffer NTI (e.g. for 200mg of agarose add 400 µL Buffer NTI, for 300mg of agarose add 600 µL Buffer NTI). 3. Incubate sample for 10 minutes at 50°C using Thermomixer. Vortex the sample briefly every 2 – 3 minutes until the gel slice is completely dissolved. 4. Place a NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Column into a Collection Tube and load up to 700 µL sample. 5. Centrifuge for 1 minute at 11,000 x g. Discard flow-through and place column back into collection tube. Load remaining sample if necessary and centrifuge for 1 minute at 11,000 x g. 6. Add 700 µL Wash Buffer NT3 to the NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Column. Centrifuge for 1 minute at 11,000 x g. Discard flow-through and place column back into the collection tube. 7. For a second time, add 700 µL Wash Buffer NT3 to the NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Column. Centrifuge for 1 minute at 11,000 g. Discard flow-through and place the column back into the empty collection tube. 8. Centrifuge empty tubes for 2 minutes at 11,000 x g to remove residual Wash Buffer NT3. Make sure spin column does not come in contact with flow-through while removing it from collection tube. 9. Place NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Column into a new 1.5mL microcentrifuge tube. 10. Add 40 µL Buffer NE and incubate at room temperature for 1 minute. 11. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 11,000 x g.

steps.title: Decontaminate work area
steps.instruction: Clean the bench and all pipettes with an RNase‑decontamination solution (e.g., RNase AWAY™) before handling any RNA.

steps.title: Prepare negative control
steps.instruction: Set aside normal human plasma (NHP) or buffer to serve as a negative control for contamination testing.

steps.title: Make carrier‑RNA stock
steps.instruction: Add 310 µL RNase‑free water to the 310 µg lyophilized carrier RNA supplied with the PureLink® Viral RNA/DNA Mini Kit, mix thoroughly, aliquot, and store at –20 °C (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Prepare lysis‑buffer/Carrier mix
steps.instruction: Thaw the required volume of 1 µg/µL carrier‑RNA stock and add it to the lysis buffer according to the number of samples (e.g., for 1 run: 210 µL Lysis Buffer + 6 µL Carrier RNA; for 6 runs: 1260 µL + 35 µL; for 10 runs: 2100 µL + 59 µL; for 24 runs: 5040 µL + 141 µL). Mix gently by pipetting; do not vortex.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL Proteinase K (included with the kit) to a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add sample
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL cell‑free sample (room‑temperature) to the tube; if the sample volume is <200 µL, bring the total volume to 200 µL with PBS or 0.9 % NaCl.

steps.title: Lyse sample
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL prepared Lysis Buffer/Carrier RNA mix, close the lid, vortex 15 s, then incubate at 56 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Add ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL 96–100 % ethanol (final ethanol concentration ≈37 %), vortex 15 s, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then briefly centrifuge to collect droplets.

steps.title: Bind nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate‑ethanol mixture (~675 µL) onto a Viral Spin Column, centrifuge at 6 800 × g for 1 min, discard the flow‑through and place the column in a clean 2 mL Wash Tube.

steps.title: Wash spin column
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with Wash Buffer II containing ethanol as follows:

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer II + ethanol, centrifuge 6 800 × g for 1 min, discard flow‑through.
Repeat the above wash a second time.
Repeat the above wash a third time.

steps.title: Dry membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the spin column to a clean Wash Tube, centrifuge at maximum speed in a microcentrifuge for 1 min to dry the membrane, then discard the Wash Tube.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Place the column in a clean 1.5 mL Recovery Tube, add 50 µL sterile RNase‑free water to the center of the membrane, incubate 1 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 min. Collect the eluate (purified viral RNA/DNA) and store at –80 °C or use immediately.

steps.title: Set up RT primer
steps.instruction: In a PCR hood (Pre‑PCR area), dispense 1 µL of primer R‑RT‑NcoI4363 (10 µM) into each PCR tube.

steps.title: Add RNA template
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of the purified RNA sample to each tube containing the primer.

steps.title: Initial RT incubation
steps.instruction: Run the one‑step RT‑PCR program “RNA 65” on a GeneAmp® 9700: 5 min at 65 °C (total volume 6 µL).

steps.title: Cool RT mix
steps.instruction: Transfer the primer/RNA mixture to a purple cooling box and chill for 2 min.

steps.title: Prepare RT‑PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix for n + 1 reactions (see Document RT‑PCR‑MM) containing:

substeps.instruction: 25 µL Herculase II RT‑PCR 2× Master Mix
1 µL Affinity Script RT/RNase Block (keep refrigerated).
Keep the master mix on ice.

steps.title: Add master mix to tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 44 µL of the master mix into each PCR tube (now total volume 50 µL).

steps.title: Run one‑step RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Run program “PR‑RT‑PCR1” on the GeneAmp® 9700:

steps.title: ExoProStar treatment
steps.instruction: On ice in the Post‑PCR area, add 5 µL ExoProStar™ to each first‑PCR product (mix tube by flicking), then run program “Exostar” on the GeneAmp® 9700:

steps.title: Prepare second‑PCR mix
steps.instruction: In a PCR hood, prepare a mix for n + 1 reactions (keep on ice) containing:

steps.title: Add second‑PCR mix
steps.instruction: Dispense 45 µL of the second‑PCR mix into each fresh PCR tube (kept in the cooling box).

steps.title: Add first‑PCR product
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of the ExoProStar‑treated first‑round PCR product to each tube.

steps.title: Run second‑PCR
steps.instruction: Run program “PR‑RT‑PCR2” on the GeneAmp® 9700:

steps.title: Prepare agarose gel
steps.instruction: Weigh agarose (e.g., 1 g for a 1 % gel) and mix with 1× TBE buffer to the desired final volume (400 mL for a full‑size gel, 100 mL for a cassette). Add ethidium bromide only in a dedicated area while wearing nitrile gloves; dispose of waste appropriately.

steps.title: Defrost and dilute sequencing primers
steps.instruction: Defrost primers and prepare a 1 : 100 dilution by mixing 1 µL primer with 99 µL RNase‑free water in the Pre‑PCR room.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing reaction mix
steps.instruction: In the main lab, make a mix for n + 1 reactions containing:

substeps.instruction: 3 µL primer (1 µM) – choose F‑2005, F‑2135, F‑2610, R‑2605, R‑3010 or R‑3584 as required
Add RNase‑free water to bring the total volume to 20 µL.

steps.title: Set up sequencing reactions
steps.instruction: Dispense Y µL of the sequencing mix into each fresh PCR tube, add Z µL of the corresponding PCR product, then run program “SEQ.REAK” on the GeneAmp® 9700:

steps.title: Prepare Sephadex purification plate
steps.instruction: Fill a black metal plate with Sephadex powder (compact with a spatula), flip onto a filter plate, and tap to transfer the powder into the wells.

steps.title: Swell Sephadex
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL DNase‑free deionised water to each well (avoid touching the Sephadex), then let swell for 3–4 h at room temperature (or 30 min at 37 °C).

steps.title: Centrifuge Sephadex plate (first spin)
steps.instruction: Fix the Sephadex plate to the collection plate with the blue rubber adapter and centrifuge 5 min at 600 × g. Discard the water.

steps.title: Apply sequencing samples
steps.instruction: Place the Sephadex plate back on the collection plate, pipette each sequencing reaction onto the Sephadex (avoid touching the resin), secure with tape, then centrifuge 5 min at 900 × g and collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: Store purified sequencing products
steps.instruction: Discard the used water, keep the Sephadex plates, and store the purified sequencing reactions at +4 °C covered with Saran‑wrap. If fewer than four wells are filled, add 20 µL water to empty wells to avoid capillary damage.

steps.title: Start sequencer software
steps.instruction: Open “Run 3130 Data Collection v3.0”, verify that all applications turn from red (off) to green (on).

steps.title: Load sample plate
steps.instruction: Place the sealed 96‑well plate (four wells per capillary; fill empty wells with 20 µL water) onto the autosampler, ensuring the notched end of the plate base points away from you.

steps.title: Seal plate with septa
steps.instruction: Align the septa strip holes with the plate wells, press firmly to seal, inspect for bubbles, and briefly centrifuge the plate if needed.

steps.title: Assemble plate assembly
steps.instruction: Insert the sealed plate into the plate base, snap on the plate retainer, and confirm that the retainer and septa holes are aligned; re‑assemble if misaligned.

steps.title: Insert plate into instrument
steps.instruction: Close the oven and front doors, press the Tray button until the autosampler stops at the forward position, open the front doors, place the plate assembly on the autosampler, then close the instrument doors.

steps.title: Run sequencing
steps.instruction: In the Data Collection software, click the green arrow, confirm the Processing Plates dialog, and start the run (the instrument may pause briefly to reach oven temperature).
